Polaris Meteor Watch & UFO Evening

Polaris Meteor Watch & UFO Evening Celebration

Celebrate the solstice week by gathering with neighbors to observe meteor showers near Polaris, blending celestial wonder with folk UFO traditions.

  1. Afternoon / 4:00 pm

    Decorate with Neon Saucer Lanterns

    Hang neon saucer lanterns around your home and yard to welcome guests and create a festive, otherworldly atmosphere that honors UFO lore.

  2. Early Evening / 6:00 pm

    Set Up Telescopes and Laser Pointer

    Align telescopes facing north towards Polaris and prepare a laser pointer to trace the Little Dipper constellation, inviting children to learn and explore the night sky.

  3. Evening / 7:30 pm

    Meteor-Counting and Synth Carol Music

    Lead children in keeping meteor-counting logs while playing synth carols in the background to enhance the celestial ambiance.

  4. Night / 8:30 pm

    Enjoy Citrus-Rosemary Popcorn

    Snack on citrus-rosemary popcorn, a bright and fragrant treat that complements the evening’s fresh air and stargazing experience.

    Recipes: Citrus-Rosemary Popcorn

  5. Night / 9:30 pm

    Share Smoky Chili Dinner

    Gather around for a hearty serving of smoky chili, perfect for warming up as you watch the meteor showers and share stories.

    Recipes: Smoky Chili

  6. Late Night / 11:00 pm

    Sip Midnight Cocoa

    Pour midnight cocoa tinted nebula-blue and sip slowly while continuing to watch the skies and enjoy the company of friends and family.

    Recipes: Midnight Cocoa

  7. Midnight / 12:00 am

    Stardust Shortbread Saucers Dessert

    Conclude the evening with shortbread saucers dusted with edible stardust, symbolizing the sparkling sky and the magic of the festival.

    Recipes: Shortbread Saucers

End the magical night feeling connected to the cosmos and your community under the watchful glow of Polaris.
